themes_detail.label: Worship Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Houses of worship noise complaints exploded to 4 this week compared to a 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (3100% spike, z-score 11.72), suggesting either a new venue operating at disruptive hours or amplified activity in this week alone that warrants immediate investigation into which institution and what changed.
evidence: 4 noise complaints from houses of worship THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% increase)
Z-score of 11.72 indicates statistically extreme deviation
This is the single highest spike across all 311 categories tracked
reporting_angles: Which house of worship in Tottenville/Great Kills is generating complaints, and has there been a recent event, expansion, or change in operating hours?
Are residents reporting the same venue multiple times, or multiple different religious institutions?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 208 this week versus a 57.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (265% spike, z-score 10.7), suggesting a rapid deterioration of road surfaces across the district that coincides with recent heavy weather or delayed maintenance response.
evidence: 208 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 57.0 weekly average (265% increase, z-score 10.7)
Street condition is the 3rd most common complaint category overall (1430 in 90 days) and now accelerating sharply
Community Board has requested street reconstruction funding year after year, indicating chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Which streets are being reported most frequently? Are potholes, flooding, or subsidence the primary complaint?
Has DOT acknowledged the spike and deployed repair crews, or are residents waiting?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees & Branches
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 22 this week versus a 4.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (450% spike, z-score 6.17), aligning with both recent weather damage and the Community Board's repeated unfunded requests for forestry services.
evidence: 22 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly baseline (450% increase, z-score 6.17)
Damaged trees are already 400 complaints in 90 days (9th largest complaint category)
Community Board has requested forestry services funding repeatedly in budget requests—indicates systemic underresourcing
reporting_angles: Are the complaints concentrated in specific neighborhoods, or distributed across Tottenville and Great Kills?
Is Parks Department able to respond to the volume, or are residents facing unsafe overhanging branches near homes and streets?

themes_detail.label: Homeless Encampments & Assistance Requests
themes_detail.summary: Homeless encampment complaints appeared in 3 reports two weeks ago (2300% spike from 0.1 baseline, z-score 8.69) and homeless person assistance requests hit 4 last week versus 0.2 weekly average (1500% spike, z-score 8.66), suggesting either a new visible encampment or heightened reporting of unsheltered populations in the district.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 baseline (2300% spike, z-score 8.69)
4 homeless person assistance requests last week vs. 0.2 baseline (1500% spike, z-score 8.66)
Community Board requests outreach services and elder assistance programs annually, indicating existing service gaps
reporting_angles: Where are encampments located (parks, streets, industrial areas) and what services are available to unhoused residents?
Are 311 reports coming from residents, city outreach workers, or both? What triggers an assistance request vs. a complaint?

themes_detail.label: Derelict & Abandoned Vehicles
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints spiked to 14 last week versus a 2.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (387% spike, z-score 5.49), while abandoned vehicles remain a top complaint (350 in 90 days, 7th largest), suggesting persistent vehicle abandonment and slow city removal response in an industrial-zoned area.
evidence: 14 derelict vehicle complaints last week vs. 2.9 weekly baseline (387% increase, z-score 5.49)
Abandoned vehicles are the 7th most common complaint type overall (350 in 90 days)
Community Board requests enforcement of illegal dumping laws annually, suggesting known enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: Are derelict vehicles concentrated near the South Shore Industrial Center or scattered across residential areas?
What is the NYPD/Sanitation removal timeline when a derelict vehicle is reported?
